paper_title: Plastic Solar Cells: A Multidisciplinary Field To Construct Chemical Concepts from Current Research

knowledge_points.content: The standard measurement conditions for terrestrial organic solar cells are defined as a light intensity of 1000 W/m², a spectral distribution of AM 1.5 global standard solar spectrum, and a working temperature of 25 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: These conditions (for terrestrial solar cells) use a light intensity of 1000 W m−2 and a spectral distribution AM 1.5 global standard solar spectrum... The working temperature is defined as 25 °C.

knowledge_points.content: The fill factor (FF) of an organic solar cell is the ratio of the maximum power (Pmax) to the product of short-circuit current (Isc) and open-circuit voltage (Voc), representing the 'squareness' of the I-V curve.
knowledge_points.evidence: Division of Pmax by the product of ISC and VOC yields the filling factor, FF... The FF is a quality consideration, as it measures the 'squareness' of the I-V curve.

knowledge_points.content: In organic semiconductors, an exciton is a bound state of an electron and a hole held together by Coulomb force, which requires photons with energy equal to or higher than the bandgap (hν ≥ Eg) for photogeneration.
knowledge_points.evidence: In an insulator or semiconductor, an exciton is an excited state that corresponds to a bound state of an electron, e− and an imaginary particle called an electron hole, h+... both remain bounded by a Coulomb force... only photons higher in energy than the band gap (hν ≥ Eg) contribute to the photogeneration.

knowledge_points.content: The bulk heterojunction (BHJ) architecture is designed to maximize the donor-acceptor (D-A) interface throughout the material, ideally ensuring that every point in the composite is within the exciton diffusion length of an interface.
knowledge_points.evidence: Conceptually, a bulk heterojunction is a multiple D-A junction in which the D-A interface is present everywhere in the material... In an ideal situation, any point in the composite is within a few nanometers of a D-A interface (i.e., within the exciton diffusion length).

knowledge_points.content: Intrinsic charge carrier mobilities in organic materials typically range from 10⁻⁷ to 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, with electron-transporting materials often exhibiting even lower values due to high structural disorder.
knowledge_points.evidence: One important limitation to the use of organic materials in solar cells lies in their low intrinsic mobilities, which range typically between 10−7 and 10−3 cm2 V−1 s−1 for hole-transporting materials and are even smaller for electron transporters. One of the reasons for the low mobility is the high disorder of most organic solids.

knowledge_points.content: The use of discotic liquid crystals, such as hexaperibenzocoronene combined with perylenebisimide derivatives, facilitates highly ordered thin films where π-π overlapping creates continuous pathways for charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: This strategy has been used by Mullen and coworkers (Figure 3) to combine the electron-donor discotic liquid crystal hexaperibenzocoronene and perylenebisimide derivatives (acceptors) to produce highly ordered thin films... the π-π overlapping between planar-conjugated molecules created a vertical and continuous 'highway' for the transport of carriers.

knowledge_points.content: Optimal power conversion efficiency in organic solar cells requires small bandgap materials (Eg ≈ 1.1 eV) to better match the broad absorption range of the solar emission spectrum.
knowledge_points.evidence: This flexibility in chemical tailoring is essential for matching the absorption spectrum of the photoactive material to the solar emission spectrum... Therefore, small bandgap materials (Eg ca. 1.1 eV) are more suitable for optimized efficiencies.

knowledge_points.content: The selection of solvent significantly impacts device performance; for example, using chlorobenzene instead of toluene for the active layer spin-casting can increase power conversion efficiency from 0.9% to 2.5% due to enhanced film uniformity.
knowledge_points.evidence: The power conversion efficiency increased from 0.9% when the active layer was cast from toluene to 2.5% when chlorobenzene was used instead... the enhanced uniformity of the film obtained from chlorobenzene solutions could dramatically produce a change in the performance of the cell.

knowledge_points.content: The 'double cable' polymer approach involves covalently linking electron-acceptor moieties (like [60]fullerene) directly to a donor polymer backbone to prevent phase segregation and enable simultaneous n-type and p-type conduction.
knowledge_points.evidence: This is the so-called 'double cable' approach due to their p- or n-type conduction properties, that is, electron transport through the 'cable' formed by the acceptor units and hole transport through the polymeric chain 'cable'... This approach is intended to overcome phase segregation.

knowledge_points.content: Donor-acceptor diblock copolymers can be used to control domain sizes at the nanometer scale through self-organization, sometimes resulting in unique morphologies like honeycomb structures.
knowledge_points.evidence: Donor-acceptor diblock copolymers (Figure 5C) have also been proposed... domain sizes can be controlled down to the nanometer scale... The polymer structure results in the formation of a honeycomb structure on the micrometer scale.
